record.context_brief: MDM for a stadium; horseshoe thresholds
record.original_question: Fix r > 0. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. Let M be an R-stadium, defined as the boundary of the R-neighborhood of a segment. For parameters satisfying r < R < 5r, describe the set of maximal distance minimizers for this R-stadium. Additionally, determine (i) the supremum of constants C such that there exists a maximal distance minimizer for a Cr-neighborhood that is not a horseshoe, and (ii) the infimum of constants c such that for any closed curve with minimal radius of curvature cr, every maximal distance minimizer is a horseshoe.

evidence.quote:
For a given compact set M ⊂ Rd and a given positive number r > 0, consider the problem of finding a connected compact
set Σ of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H1 ) such that

                                M ⊂ Br (Σ),

where Br (Σ) denotes the closed r-neighborhood of the set Σ. We refer to such a set Σ as a Maximal distance minimizer
(MDM or r-minimizer).

Question 1.2. What is the set of maximal distance minimizers for R-stadium (which is the boundary of R-neighborhood
of a segment)? Open for r < R < 5r.

Thus the following sub-questions remain open:
    • To find the supremum of C such that there exists MDM for Cr-neighborhood which is not horseshoe.
    • To find the infimum of c such that for any closed curve with minimal radius of curvature cr every MDM is horseshoe.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix r > 0 and work in the Euclidean plane (or, more generally, in R^d). For a compact set M ⊂ R^d, a maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for M is a connected compact set Σ ⊂ R^d that minimizes the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(Σ) subject to the covering constraint M ⊂ B_r(Σ), where B_r(Σ) = {x : dist(x, Σ) ≤ r} is the closed r-neighborhood of Σ. A horseshoe (for a closed convex curve of "inner offset" radius R − r) is a set obtained as the union of an arc of a curve parallel to the given one at distance r, together with two straight segments tangent to that arc.

Let R > 0 and let M = ∂(B_R(I)) be the R-stadium, i.e. the boundary of the closed R-neighborhood of a line segment I ⊂ R^2 of positive length.

(a) For every pair (r, R) with r < R < 5r, describe completely the set of maximal distance minimizers Σ associated with the R-stadium M.

(b) Determine the supremum of those constants C > 0 for which there exists a compact convex set whose boundary is a smooth closed curve and whose Cr-neighborhood admits a maximal distance minimizer that is not a horseshoe.

(c) Determine the infimum of those constants c > 0 such that, for every closed convex curve in the plane whose minimal radius of curvature is at least cr, every maximal distance minimizer of that curve is a horseshoe.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly listed as open. The horseshoe conjecture for circles is confirmed for R > 4.98r; for the stadium it is known that minimizers are horseshoes when R > 5r and not horseshoes when R < 1.75r, leaving the regime r < R < 5r unresolved. The sharp constants C and c remain undetermined in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On the horseshoe conjecture for maximal distance minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: Miranda–Paolini–Stepanov conjectured every minimizer for a circle of radius R>r is a horseshoe; confirmed for R>4.98r.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: Question on R-stadium MDM open for r<R<5r; sub-questions on sharp constants C and c remain open.

status_evidence.title: Maximal distance minimizers for a rectangle
status_evidence.snippet: Related result on MDM for rectangles with stadium-type analysis.
